# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and why it is not aliases_src/{lang}_curated.tsv
# Those files are inputs to the BUNDLE BUILD (indicator/fhir/embeddings/
# lexicon.py). Their right-hand side is a descriptive English phrase —
# "Total cholesterol TC", "Leukocyte count WBC" — which is exactly the shape
# This file serves the OFFLINE RESOLVER at runtime, where the right-hand side
# has a different job: it must itself be a key the finished alias index can
# look up. "Total cholesterol TC" is a fine build input and a dead end at
# lookup time. Rewriting the build inputs to suit the resolver would have
# quietly degraded the semantic pipeline, so the two concerns get two files.
# Every row here was a documented failure in test_engine_coverage.py. Two
# kinds of failure appear, and the second is the dangerous one:
#   MISS  — "LDL cholesterol" resolved to nothing. The index is built from
#           LOINC long common names, so it knows the formal name and the lab
#           short code (LDL-C) but not the phrase humans write. Plain English
#   WRONG — "血红蛋白" resolved to Hemoglobin A1c: a different test, returned
#           with full confidence. It matches 301 index rows and the commonness
#           prior likes HbA1c best. A resolution-rate metric scores this as a
#           success; a patient reading the report would not.
# CONTRIBUTING: this is the lowest-barrier useful PR in the repo. Find a term
# that resolves wrong or not at all, add one row here plus one case in
# mirobody/test_engine_coverage.py, and raise COVERAGE_FLOOR. Any language.
# Targets are validated by the test suite, so a typo'd target fails CI rather
# The bare plural nouns (Leukocytes, Erythrocytes, Hematocrit) are not index
# keys on their own; the LOINC short names are. "HCT" alone is not usable as
# a target either — it collides with Calcitonin.

column1: # The short codes a CBC / 生化 printout puts in its own column. They were the
# worst-covered surface in the resolver, and two of them were WRONG rather than
# missing — the same near-miss class as 血红蛋白 -> HbA1c, just wearing the
#   HGB -> 4548-4  Hemoglobin A1c        (a diabetes marker for a CBC line)
#   HCT -> 1992-7  Calcitonin            (a thyroid hormone for hematocrit)
# Targets are the phrasings the index actually keys on; each row was checked
# with `mirobody resolve` before being written down.
# Abbreviations that name more than one test resolve to the WIDESPREAD
# reading rather than refusing. A panel name is a different case and stays
# blocked (see the non-answers section): there, no single observation code
# can be right. Here one reading dominates ordinary use by a wide margin,
# and an honest miss on `CA` helps nobody when 钙 is what a 生化 panel means
# by it ~always. What must not happen is the index picking for us — that is
# how HGB became HbA1c — so each is written down.
#   CA = 钙 (calcium), not 癌抗原 CA-125/CA19-9 (those spell themselves out)
#   PT = 凝血酶原时间 (prothrombin time), not 前列腺素 / 甲状旁腺
#   MG = 镁 (magnesium), not the unit mg
#   Cr = 肌酐 (creatinine), not chromium — and note `Cr`/`CR` casefold to one
#        key, so only one row can win
# ══ 日本語 — 健康診断 terms the ja.tsv sweep does not carry ═══════════════════
# ja.tsv is 16,809 rows but its right-hand side is overwhelmingly SNOMED-shaped:
# diseases and organisms (Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus, Ornithine
# transcarbamoylase deficiency), not LOINC observations — only 3% of its
# distinct targets are keys the observation index can look up. Everyday 健康診断
# names come out at 20/24 all the same, via zh/ja_curated plus the index; these
# four are what a spot-check of the panel found missing.
# HRV is heart rate variability. It is also the abbreviation for human
# rhinovirus, and the index preferred that reading: `HRV` answered 40991-2
# Rhinovirus+Enterovirus RNA, a PCR panel, for what every wearable on the
# market means by those three letters. Same rule as CA/PT/MG above: the
# widespread reading, written down rather than left to the commonness prior.
# The code is 112429-6, which is also what the catalogue's `hrvSDNN` carries,
# so a wearable reading and a written one group together (owner, 2026-09-22).
# LOINC has no unqualified-HRV code: all three candidates are SDNN. The other
# two assert more than the bare word does, 76643-6 a METHOD of EKG and both of
# them SYSTEM=Heart, and no text reaches them now (measured: naming the EKG
# abstains, and so does their own long common name).
# 凝血酶原时间 answered 34714-6 INR: a DERIVED ratio, not the time itself.
# ══ panel terms that DO have a panel code ═════════════════════════════════
# "blood pressure" written on its own. All four spellings below name the same
# concept and, before this block existed, got three different answers:
#   血圧              -> nothing  (no entry in any language file)
#   blood pressure    -> blocked  (the index answered 8462-4, DIASTOLIC — a
#                                  systolic reading filed under it lands in the
#                                  wrong series, which is why it was blocked)
# The eval harness asked why one language got a code and another got silence,
# and there was no reason. But unifying them exposed the worse bug: 18684-1 is
# not a blood-pressure panel. Its axis reads PROPERTY=Cmplx, SCALE=Set,
# CLASS=ATTACH.ED — an emergency-department ATTACHMENT code, a document, not a
# measurement. Its LONG_COMMON_NAME just happens to read "First Blood pressure
# Set". So the language that "worked" was returning a document code with full
# 85354-9 is the real answer: CLASS=PANEL.VITALS, and it is the code FHIR R4's
# vital-signs profile mandates for blood pressure, with 8480-6 / 8462-4 as its
# components. A caller who wants one number still has to say which — that is
# what a panel code means — but now they are told that, instead of being handed
# either silence or an ED attachment.
# `blood_pressure` needs no row: underscore flattening reaches "blood pressure".
# It is pinned in test_engine_coverage.py anyway, because that flattening is
# exactly the route that used to walk around the old block.

column1: # `Hepatitis B virus e Ag` is the LOINC COMPONENT, not a corpus name, so this
# row pointed at nothing and 乙肝e抗原 answered nothing for as long as it
# existed. Its four neighbours happen to name targets the corpus does carry,
# which is why the file looked fine. `test_overrides_are_live` now checks
# every row's target instead of trusting the shape.
# 血型 answered 50962-0 "XXX blood group IgG Ab [Titer]" — an antibody titre,
# not a blood type. ABO grouping is 883-9.
# ── the CBC differential: percent vs absolute ────────────────────────────────
# LOINC models a differential percentage as a RATIO ANALYTE — COMPONENT
# `neutrophils/leukocytes`, PROPERTY NFr — not as another property of
# `neutrophils`. That is why `variant_for_reading` cannot reach it: it searches
# siblings sharing the FULL component, which is right for cholesterol
# (`cholesterol` MCnc vs SCnc, one component, two properties) and structurally
# It cannot be inferred either: `neutrophils` has three NFr children —
# `/cells`, `/leukocytes`, `/round cells` — and only clinical knowledge picks
# the CBC one. So the mapping is written down, which is what this file is for.
# 中性粒细胞 was the odd one out: its four panel siblings all resolved to the
# `X/Leukocytes` ratio while it resolved to `[#/volume]`. Five lines of one
# panel now behave the same way, and a report that says 62 and one that says
# 4.2 no longer land on one series in two units.
# Traditional spellings need no rows — `surface_variants` folds zh-Hant to
# zh-Hans and finds these. `中性粒细胞%` needs none either: the bare form is
# The other half of the distinction. `绝对值` is one CJK token, so unlike `%`
# it produces no bare-stem variant and needs its own row.
# The target names the METHOD-LESS code explicitly. Pointing at bare
# `Neutrophils` lands on 751-8 `… by Automated count`, and the unit-driven
# crossing in `variant_for_reading` prefers the method-less 26499-4 — so the
# same measurement got two identities depending on whether the report spelled
# out 绝对值 or printed a bare name with 10*9/L, which is exactly the split
# these rows exist to prevent. Both routes now end on the same code, and it is
# the method-less one for the reason that function already states: `by
# Automated count` is a narrower claim than a report saying "4.2" supports.
# The same distinction on the English side, which was still inverted.
# `surface_variants` strips a trailing `#` or `%` to a bare stem, so `NEUT#`
# and `NEUT%` both reach `neut`. In Chinese the bare stem carries a row above
# and lands on the ratio, which is why `中性粒细胞%` is already right. English
# has no such row: `neut` matched the index at 751-8 `[#/volume] by Automated
# count`, so `NEUT%` answered an ABSOLUTE code and `LYMPH#` a PERCENTAGE one.
# Exact-surface rows win because variants are tried most-specific first.
# Targets are the method-less codes the rows above use, so a report printing
# NEUT# and one printing 中性粒细胞绝对值 land on one series.
# `Hemoglobin A1c` — the full English name — was the only one of four spellings
# that answered 41995-2 (a mass concentration almost no report means) while
# 糖化血红蛋白 / HbA1c / A1c all answered 4548-4, the ratio every lab prints as a
# percentage. The outlier was the spelling an English document is most likely
# 呼吸频率 is the standard Chinese vital-sign term and did not resolve at all;
# 呼吸速率 resolved to 9278-3 `Breath rate special circumstances`, which is a
# ventilator/exercise-protocol code, not the number on a vitals panel. Only the
# bare 呼吸 worked, which is the spelling a report is least likely to print.
# ── everyday panel terms, swept against a 132-term Chinese report vocabulary ─
# 27 of 132 did not resolve (20%), and the misses were not exotic: they were
# the FULL spelling of a term whose abbreviation already worked. A formal
# report prints 乙型肝炎表面抗原; a summary prints 乙肝表面抗原; only the second
# resolved. Same shape for 丙型肝炎抗体/丙肝抗体, 血肌酐/肌酐, 三酰甘油/甘油三酯.
# The infectious-disease panel was the worst of it — 12 of its 26 spellings
# missing — and it is on nearly every physical-examination report there is.

# appears inside that code's own name. A wrong answer, not a missing one, and

# written with NO space, which is how a table cell renders it, and which the
